events.notes: Both labellers agree: put down at 43 s and unattended at 48 s. The owner is a man in a striped grey T-shirt, khaki trousers and red/blue shoes. The merged box [125,310,190,375] is the tighter combination of L1 [125,315,190,375] and L2 [120,305,190,375]. I checked it on full-resolution frames. At 50 s the bag is upright at about x126-170, y312-375, strap included, and fits inside the box. At 61 s, the middle of the unattended period, it has toppled and lies at about x130-188, y325-375, also inside the box. Disputed point 1: L1 says a person who looks like the owner comes back at 66-70 s, while L2 says the owner never comes back. Checking the 68 s frame confirms that the owner (same striped shirt, khaki trousers and red/blue shoes) walks across the far right of the scene at about x440-530. He never goes near the bag or touches it, so owner_returns=false: he reappears but does not reclaim the bag. Disputed point 2: the round table position is only a scene note, not part of the event; it is settled in scene_notes. Passers-by in a checked shirt and a red/white striped polo (at about 50, 60-62 and 68-71 s) do not touch the bag.

events.notes: Both labellers agreed on the same event: a man in a brown jacket enters at about 63 s, sets a black bag down at the base of the thin pole left of the silver bollard at about 69.5 s, walks off toward the top of the frame and is gone by about 74 s. The bag stays until the end of the video (94 s), and a later person near the scooter does not take it. Disputes: (1) t_unattended was 72 vs 73 s. At 71 s the owner is only about 1 body height (~60 px) above the bag, so it becomes unattended between 72 and 73 s; I used the average, 72.5. (2) The boxes were [456,72,484,110] vs [458,78,478,112]. I checked a zoomed full-resolution frame at 83 s (middle of the unattended period). The dark bag spans about x 456-479 and y 73-110. L1's right edge of 484 runs into the pole, and L2's box cuts off the top of the bag, so I used [456,73,479,110].

A woman with a backpack walks through from about 68 to 76 s and leaves nothing. From about 82 s a rider parks a white scooter at the top right (a vehicle, not an abandoned object) and stays nearby until the end, near the bag but without touching it.

events.notes: Both labellers agree on the object, put-down time (56 s), that it is never removed (it stays until the end at 87 s, frame 2608), and that the owner returns. The man in the brown jacket and pink shirt walks back down from the top at about 84 s but has not reached the bag when the clip ends. The only difference was t_unattended: labeller 1 said 68 s and labeller 2 said 71 s, which is within the 3 s tolerance. I checked the full-resolution frame at 70 s: the owner's feet are at about y=92 and the bag is at about y=230, roughly 140-150 px apart. His body is about 90-110 px tall, so the 2-body-height threshold is reached at about 70 s, which matches the average (69.5 s). I set it to 70 s. The two boxes almost match ([212,214,258,248] and [212,212,258,248]), so I merged them to [212,213,258,248]. I checked this box on the full-resolution frame at 78 s, the middle of the unattended period, and it fits the bag tightly. The woman with the pink umbrella and trolley passes from 76 to 86 s without touching the bag.

A woman with a pink umbrella and a shopping trolley passes at 76-86 s and keeps the trolley. The owner comes back into view at 84-87 s.

events.notes: Both labellers found the same single event, so the two were merged. A man in white carries the box in and sets it on the floor near (150,215). Owner lingers within ~1-1.5 body heights from ~38 to 65 s, then walks off toward bottom-left and leaves view. Box stays until end (~110 s); nobody else touches it. Disputes and how they were settled: (1) put_down was given as 38 and 37.5. Full-res frames show the box still in his hand, lowered near the floor, at 37.0 s and resting on the floor at 37.5 s, so I set 37.3. (2) unattended was given as 68 and 66.5. At 66 s the owner is standing over the box and blocking it from view. At 67 s he is about 1 body height away (~90 px, body ~90 px) and walking off. At 68 s he is about 2 body heights away at the bottom of the frame. I set 67.5, the point where he passes the ~2-body-height threshold, which falls between the two labels. (3) The boxes were nearly identical, [136,199,172,230] and [135,200,172,229]. On a 4x zoomed full-res crop at 89 s (middle of the unattended period), the white object fills about x 137-170 and y 202-227, so the tightened box is [136,201,171,228]. Object is small (~35x27 px) and sits on a dark floor stripe.

events.notes: The labellers agreed on the object, the location (top of the middle-right desk, not the floor), that the bag is never removed, and that the owner does not return. They differed on t_put_down (32 vs 34) and t_unattended (40 vs 38.5). Both differences are within 3 s, so the times would normally be averaged (33 / 39.25). I checked full-resolution frames to decide. At 31 s the bag is still held up above the desk. At 32 s it is resting on the desk with the hand still on the handle, which is also the case at 34 s. So put-down is 32 s, not the averaged 33 s, and Labeller 2's 34 s is when the hand releases rather than when the bag touches down. At 35 s the hand has let go and the man is turning away. At 38 s he is at about x 190-290, around 200 px from the bag. At 39 s he is at the far left (x about 60-130), more than 2 body heights from the bag. He leaves the frame at about 40 s. So t_unattended is 39 s, which agrees with the 39.25 average. The box is the intersection of both labellers' boxes, slightly tightened. On the full-resolution frame at 61 s (middle of the unattended period, 39-82.9 s), [416,136,478,209] fits the bag closely.

video11.scene_notes:
This is a crowded indoor station hall with a checkerboard floor, filmed from a high angle at 640x480 and 30 fps for 150 s. The lighting is bright and even, with glare from the shopfronts at the back. Queues stand behind the stanchions and red ropes on the left the whole time, and pedestrians pass constantly. Scene furniture present from t=0: an orange/red box or bucket at about [510,250,532,272], stanchions with red ropes, a small sign board at about [310,215,325,235], and turnstiles on the far left.

RECONCILIATION. Both labellers saw the same candidate and agree on its times and boxes. The only dispute was whether it counts as unattended. Labeller 1 included it with low confidence and a nominal t_unattended of 80 s. Labeller 2 excluded it. The candidate is two objects:
(a) A white cone-shaped object (a closed white umbrella or bag) stood upright beside a stanchion. Put down at about 26 s. Merged box [300,250,318,288].
(b) A small red bag or pouch at the foot of the next stanchion. Put down at about 40 s. Box [319,276,334,292].
I verified both boxes on a full-resolution frame at 100 s, and both fit the objects tightly. Both objects stay until the end of the video (about 150 s).

The labellers also disagreed on the owner. Labeller 1 says a woman in a white top. Labeller 2 says a man in a white shirt carrying a grey jacket. In the video, the owner is a person in a white top with a red waist bag who carries a grey jacket.

How I settled it: I checked the video at 20, 30, 45, 60, 66, 70, 74, 80, 90, 100, 110, 120, 130, 140, 145 and 149 s. At every check from 30 s to the end, the owner stands with a group of 2-3 people about 0-60 px from the objects, mostly 35-45 px to the right. That is at most about one body height, since a person there is about 50-60 px tall. The owner is never out of view and never more than about 2 body heights away. Under the unattended rule used here, the objects are attended throughout, so no event is recorded. I agree with Labeller 2. Labeller 1's 80 s value was only nominal and does not meet the rule.

Caveat: ABODA probably intends this umbrella and red bag as video11's abandoned object. If the official ABODA GT is used, take put_down as 26 s (white object) and 40 s (red bag), with the union box [300,250,334,292]. Under our rule there is still no valid unattended time.

Also not counted: a dark bag on the floor at about [404,236,420,250] from about 35 s to the end. It sits at the feet of a standing man the whole time, so it is attended. There are also many transient carried bags.
